messages:
nina: Quick sync: should the edge auto-multiplex multiple streaming requests onto a single upstream connection, or require an explicit handshake? Short thread.

omar: Auto-multiplexing helps with socket limits but causes head-of-line blocking when one stream stalls. Also complicates retries/resumes.

kevin: Can we make multiplexing opt-in from client side via a tiny handshake? Gateway returns a short-lived lane token if it agrees. Clients include token on subsequent requests.

sylvie: I like opt-in. It gives us a chance to attach metadata (resume-capable, idempotency) and enforce policy.

nina: Behavioral rules proposed:
- default: no multiplexing
- client requests multiplex via header `Prefer: multiplex`
- gateway replies `X-RW-Lane: id=abc;ttl=30s` if accepted
- gateway rejects non-replayable requests into lanes (409)

omar: Resume tokens: gateway emits a signed resume token on disconnect for lane+offset; resume only allowed if backend advertises `resume: true` in model registry.

kevin: Also add per-tenant lane quotas and short TTLs to prevent abuse. Trace tags `lane.id` added to spans for observability.

sylvie: Action items: kevin will draft header schema; omar will add resume flag in registry; nina will write a brief RFC.

deploy-bot: Canary queued: "multiplex-probe" (10 requests) https://ci.internal/jobs/7890

nina: Decision: opt-in multiplex via handshake, reject non-replayable lanes, resume only for resume-capable models, quota issuance. RFC next.
